summary: Red Line is a cozy, retro storytelling game. You play Earth, texting with three Mars robots, Ingenuity, Spirit and Opportunity. They tell their missions one moment at a time, with jokes, a few tears and real photos. Reply with a tap or ask them anything, and tap the small (i) for a quick fact.
details:
is a cozy, retro storytelling game that gives NASA’s retired Mars machines a voice.

What it does and how it works
You play Earth on a late-1990s desktop and open a chat app. Three retired explorers text you their missions: Ingenuity the helicopter, and the twin rovers Spirit and Opportunity. Each message carries a real mission date, and you reply with a tap or your own words to move the story on. Mars photos arrive in the chat and are collected in an Album. A small (i) button on each message gives a quick fact. Players can also type a question, such as “How many blades do you have?”, and the rover answers in one or two short lines, with a longer explanation behind the (i).

Benefits and intended impact
Most young space fans only hear about active missions. Red Line introduces ages 9 to 14, and casual fans, to what the machines were, why they were sent and what they discovered. For example, a dragged wheel uncovered signs of past water, and a helicopter built for five flights flew 72. We want players to feel a personal connection to these explorers, and to leave curious about the science.

Tools
Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with no frameworks or installation. We used the Canvas, SVG, Web Audio and file browser tools, and Google Fonts for the pixel text. Claude writes the answers to typed questions. Python and Node.js helped us build and check the files. The mission facts were checked against NASA sources.

Creativity
The robots tell their own stories, with humour and emotion, as texts from friends. The look is a nostalgic desktop and early social-network chat, with grain, scanlines and soft generated music, so learning feels relaxing instead of like homework.

What we considered

  • Audience: short, plain-language messages that never overload the chat.
  • Accuracy: NASA-sourced dates and facts, and a spoiler-safe timeline.
  • Honesty about AI: the story and facts are fixed text, and typed answers are labelled as AI-written.
  • Accessibility: it runs in any browser, with an optional sound switch, keyboard use and reduced-motion support.
